text:
erin: heads up — got a CS escalation from AcmeCorp about p99 latency spikes on /v1/generate after 09:00 UTC. They say tail latency jumped ~3x around 09:03 and 09:12. ticket #4521.

sam: ack. any correlation with recent runtime changes? we shipped the continuous-batcher tuning yesterday (lowered batch_timeout_ms to 10ms, increased max_batch_size to 64).

maria: I saw increased p95->p99 divergence in dashboards right after the rollout window. p95 up ~1.5x, p99 went from ~220ms to ~1.1s. throughput stable, error rate unchanged.

kai_oncall: logs look like many small requests waiting for a large seq to finish. I think heterogeneous seq lengths + bigger max_batch_size caused head-of-line blocking for some GPUs.

james_support: Customer sent a repro payload and trace-id x-trace=acme-8472. They were running lots of short chat completions (~40 tokens) and occasional long-inference jobs (~4k tokens) from the same API key.

erin: that matches classic batching tradeoff — big batches improve throughput but can increase tail latency when you mix short and long sequences. We should give CS a mitigation ASAP.

sam: immediate mitigation options: 1) lower max_batch_size to 16 (reduce wait), 2) increase batch_timeout_ms to 50 for small request lane, 3) add seq-length based routing to separate long jobs. Which is quickest?

maria: quickest is to reduce max_batch_size and enable per-route small-lane timeout. We have a dynamic-batching flag per-model: `enable_small_lane: true` — flipping it should be safe for a canary.

kai_oncall: +1. propose: canary to 5% of traffic on region-us-east1 with config: `{
  max_batch_size: 16,
  batch_timeout_ms: 25,
  enable_small_lane: true,
  small_lane_max_seq: 512
}`

james_support: can you also provide a short repro command so I can validate with the customer? they're happy to run tests.

sam: repro curl (short/long mix):
```bash
# short request (chat)
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "X-Trace: acme-8472" -d '{"input":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
# long request (single blocking example)
seq=$(python -c 'print("A"*3000)')
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -H "X-Trace: acme-8472" -d "{\"input\": \"$seq\"}" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```

erin: thanks. I'll ask Acme to run that for 5-10 minutes while we watch the p99.

maria: side analysis: GPU metrics show occasional NVLink saturation and long kernel times when long sequences run. KV-cache memory spikes too. That supports batching contention hypothesis.

sam: if canary looks good we'll roll to 100% with a staged ramp. monitor p95/p99, queue depth, and kernel-time histograms. alert if p99 > 700ms or queue_depth > 200ms.

kai_oncall: deployed canary at 09:27 to 5% — route ID: batcher-canary-20260315-01.

deploy-bot: deploy started for batcher-canary-20260315-01 (commit abc123). Rolling 5% to region us-east1.

maria: after canary: p95 dropped slightly back to baseline, p99 dropped from 1.1s -> 380ms for canary customers. queue depth variance reduced.

erin: Acme ran repro and confirmed their short requests are much snappier in canary. They requested ETA to full roll.

sam: next step risk: some pure-throughput customers could lose some token/sec efficiency. We need to keep a toggle for high-throughput tenants (dedicated pools) and not apply change to them.

james_support: customer follow-up sent: "thanks, improvement noticed — please roll for our org only if safe for throughput".

maria: rolling to 100% except exclude dedicated-tier tags. rollout start 09:42, expected finish 09:46.

kai_oncall: monitors in place. also scheduled a follow-up job to add seq-length based routing in the scheduler for longer term. Ticket created: ENG-7845.

erin: quick docs note for support: add these repro steps and recommended mitigations for mixed workloads: 1) use small_lane for chat-like short seqs, 2) set small_lane_max_seq, 3) keep max_batch_size conservative for mixed usage, 4) recommend customers use a separate API key for bulk long jobs.

sam: long-term fixes: speculative execution for short-latency lane (dispatch small batches immediately), per-request priority headers, and better batch-slicing heuristics.

maria: one more datapoint — we saw no increase in 5xx. So this was a latency distribution problem not failures. good.

kai_oncall: rollout finished 09:46. p99 global now ~320ms. closing oncall loop.

deploy-bot: deploy finished for batcher-canary-20260315-01. status: success.

erin: closing ticket with Acme after 24h observation window. thanks all. :tada:
